## Proof

**Yes**, the map $\mu$ induces such a product $\bullet$ on $H_*(A)$ with $[a]$ as a two-sided unit. Here is the complete argument.

---

### Step 1: Construction of the product $\bullet$

Since $\mu|_{A\times A}: A\times A \to A$ is well-defined (condition 1), it induces a map on homology:
$$\mu_*^A: H_*(A\times A) \longrightarrow H_*(A).$$

By the Künneth theorem (integral coefficients), there is a natural **cross product** injection
$$\times: H_p(A)\otimes H_q(A) \hookrightarrow H_{p+q}(A\times A),$$
which is split-injective (the short exact sequence $0\to \bigoplus H_p\otimes H_q \to H_n(A\times A)\to \bigoplus \operatorname{Tor}(H_p,H_q)\to 0$ splits, though not naturally). Regardless, the cross product map itself is always injective, so we may compose:

$$\bullet \;:=\; \mu_*^A \circ\, \times \;:\; H_p(A)\otimes H_q(A) \longrightarrow H_{p+q}(A).$$

This defines the product $\bullet: H_*(A)\otimes H_*(A)\to H_*(A)$.

---

### Step 2: The unit property — setup

Let $[a_n]\in H_n(A)$, represented by a cycle $z_n: \Delta^n\to A$ (a singular cycle). We must show:
$$[a]\bullet [a_n] = [a_n] \quad\text{and}\quad [a_n]\bullet [a]=[a_n] \quad\text{in } H_n(A).$$

We prove the left-unit identity $[a]\bullet[a_n]=[a_n]$; the right-unit case is identical using condition 2's symmetry $\mu(b',b)=b'$.

By definition, $[a]\bullet[a_n] = \mu_*^A([a]\times[z_n])$, where $[a]\times[z_n]\in H_n(A\times A)$ is the cross product, represented by the singular cycle $a\times z_n: \Delta^0\times\Delta^n \to A\times A$ sending the unique $0$-simplex to $a$ and applying $z_n$ on the second factor. Composing with $\mu|_{A\times A}$, the class $[a]\bullet[a_n]$ is represented by the cycle
$$\mu(a,\, z_n(-)):\Delta^n \to A.$$

---

### Step 3: Homotopy in $B$ relating $\mu(a,z_n)$ to $z_n$

Condition 3 gives $[a]=[b]$ in $H_0(B)$. Since $B$ is a CW-complex, $H_0(B)\cong \mathbb{Z}^{\pi_0(B)}$ records path components, so $a$ and $b$ lie in the **same path component** of $B$. Let $\gamma:[0,1]\to B$ be a path with $\gamma(0)=a$, $\gamma(1)=b$.

Define
$$H:[0,1]\times\Delta^n \longrightarrow B, \qquad H(t,x)=\mu\bigl(\gamma(t),\, z_n(x)\bigr).$$

This is continuous. At the endpoints:
- $H(0,x) = \mu(a, z_n(x))$,
- $H(1,x) = \mu(b, z_n(x)) = z_n(x)$, by condition 2 ($\mu(b,b')=b'$ for all $b'\in B$).

Thus $H$ is a homotopy in $B$ from $\mu(a,z_n(-))$ to $z_n(-)$. Therefore:
$$\mu_*^B\bigl([a]\times[z_n]\bigr) = [z_n] \quad\text{in } H_n(B),$$
where on the left $[a]\times[z_n]$ is now viewed in $H_n(B\times B)$ via $(i\times i)_*$, and $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ is the inclusion.

---

### Step 4: Using the retract to descend from $H_n(B)$ to $H_n(A)$

Since $A\subset B$ is a **retract**, there exists $r:B\to A$ with $r\circ i = \mathrm{id}_A$. On homology, $r_*\circ i_* = \mathrm{id}_{H_*(A)}$, so
$$i_*: H_*(A)\hookrightarrow H_*(B) \quad\text{is injective.}$$

By **naturality** of the cross product and of $\mu_*$, the following diagram commutes:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
H_n(A\times A) & \xrightarrow{\mu_*^A} & H_n(A) \\
\downarrow{\scriptstyle (i\times i)_*} & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle i_*} \\
H_n(B\times B) & \xrightarrow{\mu_*^B} & H_n(B)
\end{array}$$
(The right square commutes because $\mu\circ(i\times i) = i\circ \mu|_{A\times A}$, which holds since $\mu(A\times A)\subset A$ and $i$ is the inclusion.)

Applying this to $[a]\times[z_n]\in H_n(A\times A)$:
$$i_*\bigl(\mu_*^A([a]\times[z_n])\bigr) = \mu_*^B\bigl((i\times i)_*([a]\times[z_n])\bigr) = \mu_*^B([a]\times[z_n]) = [z_n] = i_*([z_n]).$$

Since $i_*$ is **injective**:
$$\mu_*^A([a]\times[z_n]) = [z_n] \quad\text{in } H_n(A).$$

That is, $[a]\bullet[a_n]=[a_n]$.

---

### Step 5: Right unit

The argument for $[a_n]\bullet[a]=[a_n]$ is identical, using the other half of condition 2: $\mu(b',b)=b'$ for all $b'\in B$. The same homotopy $H'(t,x)=\mu(z_n(x),\gamma(t))$ runs from $\mu(z_n,a)$ to $\mu(z_n,b)=z_n$ in $B$, and injectivity of $i_*$ descends the equality to $H_n(A)$.

---

### Conclusion

The restriction $\mu|_{A\times A}:A\times A\to A$, combined with the Künneth cross product, defines a product
$$\bullet: H_*(A)\otimes H_*(A)\to H_*(A).$$
The element $[a]\in H_0(A)$ acts as a two-sided unit: for every $[a_n]\in H_n(A)$,
$$[a]\bullet[a_n]=[a_n]\bullet[a]=[a_n].$$

The proof uses: (i) the Künneth cross product for existence of $\bullet$; (ii) $[a]=[b]$ in $H_0(B)$ to obtain a path $\gamma$ from $a$ to $b$, yielding a homotopy in $B$; (iii) naturality of $\mu_*$ to relate the homologies of $A$ and $B$; and (iv) the retract condition to ensure $i_*$ is injective, allowing the equality in $H_n(B)$ to be pulled back to $H_n(A)$.
